title: Cappadocia Wine, Pottery & Culinary Guide: Avanos & Ürgüp

quickAnswer: Cappadocia's culinary identity centers on crisp white Emir wines from [Turasan](https://www.turasan.com.tr/en/) (Ürgüp) and [Kocabağ](https://askcappadocia.com/poi/kocabag-wines) (Uçhisar), slow-cooked clay-pot testi kebab at family-run kitchens like Dibek, five-generation red-clay pottery workshops in Avanos, and Michelin-recognized dining rooms led by [Revithia](https://www.kayakapi.com/revithia), Nahita, and Lil'a that require advance reservations.

body.text: What are Cappadocia's signature local grapes and wineries?

Emir is Cappadocia's signature indigenous white grape—grown in high-altitude volcanic tuff soils to produce dry, mineral-driven wines with crisp green-apple acidity. Alongside Emir, regional producers bottle Anatolian reds like Kalecik Karası, Öküzgözü, and Boğazkere, led by Ürgüp's [Turasan Winery](https://www.turasan.com.tr/en/uzumler-ve-bolgeler/) (established 1943) and Uçhisar's [Kocabağ Winery](https://www.winewithseth.com/winewiki/kocabag-cappadocias-underground-wine-legacy/) (founded 1972).

Cappadocia's volcanic ash, 1,100-meter elevation, and wide day-to-night temperature swings preserve natural acidity that coastal Turkish vineyards rarely match. Both flagship producers welcome walk-in tastings, though they offer contrasting styles:

items: Turasan Winery (Ürgüp): Cappadocia's oldest commercial producer; try their Seneler Emir and Seneler Kalecik Karası alongside international varietals in a spacious stone tasting hall.

Kocabağ Winery (Uçhisar): Run by the Erdoğan family, Kocabağ ferments and ages indigenous Turkish grapes inside tanks carved directly into volcanic tuff rock—keeping cellar temperatures steady at 8–10°C without heavy oak masking the fruit.
Argos in Cappadocia Cellar (Uçhisar): Not a retail storefront, but its historic subterranean monastery cellar holds one of the largest Turkish wine collections in the region for dining guests.

body.text: Where do you try authentic testi kebab without tourist traps?

Order authentic testi kebab—beef or lamb slow-braised with tomatoes, peppers, and garlic inside a sealed Avanos clay jug—at long-standing kitchens like [Dibek Restaurant](https://restaurantsforkings.com/city/cappadocia/dibek-restaurant) or [Topdeck Cave Restaurant](https://wareontheglobe.com/2023/09/29/topdeck-cave-restaurant-possibly-the-best-restaurant-in-cappadocia/) in Göreme, or [Old Greek House](https://www.oldgreekhouse.com/) in Mustafapaşa. Avoid main-strip restaurants waving flaming clay pots at passersby, where pre-cooked stew is merely reheated for show.

Genuine testi kebab needs two to four hours over gentle embers so the meat turns fork-tender in its own juices before the waiter cracks the neck open tableside. Because real preparation takes time, call or message your chosen restaurant at least three to four hours ahead—or order it when you book dinner—and skip the gimmicky fire-lighting theatrics in favor of depth of flavor. Also sample mantı (tiny handmade Anatolian dumplings with yogurt and sumac) and kuru fasulye baked in earthenware pots.
Is Avanos pottery still handmade by family workshops?

Yes—while tour buses funnel crowds into massive highway showrooms, genuine multi-generation family studios in Avanos still throw red silt clay harvested from the Kızılırmak (Red River) on traditional foot-powered kick wheels. Visit [Güray Museum](https://www.guraymuze.com/en/) (five generations of the Tüysüz family) or [Chez Galip](https://chezgalip.com/) to watch working artisans without hard-sell pressure.

Avanos has practiced pottery since Hittite times. Güray Museum pairs an underground ceramic museum—displaying vessels from antiquity alongside contemporary Turkish ceramicists—with an active family studio where you can try the kick wheel yourself. If you want to buy functional tableware or decorative Iznik-style plates, ask clearly whether pieces are hand-thrown locally or cast in molds, and verify international shipping insurance before paying.
Which fine-dining restaurants require advance booking?

Book at least two to four weeks ahead during April–October for Cappadocia's Michelin-recognized dining rooms: [Revithia](https://www.kayakapi.com/revithia) (Kayakapı Premium Caves, Ürgüp), [Nahita](https://www.argosincappadocia.com/en/dine-wine/nahita) and [Seki](https://www.argosincappadocia.com/en/dine-wine/seki) (Argos in Cappadocia, Uçhisar), [Lil'a](https://www.lil-a.com.tr/en) (Museum Hotel, Uçhisar), and [Seten](https://guide.michelin.com/tr/en/nevsehir/nevsehir-merkez_2821449/restaurant/seten) (Göreme). Terrace sunset tables sell out first.

body.text: Revithia—awarded Cappadocia's first Michelin Star—operates dinner service only (18:00–00:00, closed Sundays) with a strict regional-ingredient tasting menu by Chef Duran Özdemir. Pair one fine-dining reservation with two casual village dinners across a [3-day Cappadocia itinerary](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/3-days-in-cappadocia), and check our [Kayseri vs Nevşehir airport transfer guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/cappadocia-airport-transfer) if you plan to dine in Ürgüp on arrival night.

faq.q: Do you need reservations for Turasan or Kocabağ wine tastings?
faq.a: Walk-ins are welcome daily at both Turasan in Ürgüp and Kocabağ in Uçhisar during regular tasting hours (typically 09:00–18:00/19:00). Reserve ahead only if you want a private cellar tour or are visiting with a group of six or more.

faq.q: Is vegetarian testi kebab available in Cappadocia?
faq.a: Yes. Most traditional restaurants—including Dibek and Seten—prepare a vegetarian clay-pot version with eggplant, mushrooms, peppers, tomatoes, and chickpeas when requested in advance.

faq.q: Can you take Cappadocia wine home on a domestic flight?
faq.a: You cannot carry wine bottles through cabin security, but you can pack bottles inside checked luggage on flights out of Kayseri (ASR) or Nevşehir (NAV). Both Turasan and Kocabağ wrap bottles in protective foam sleeves on request.

faq.q: How much does a Michelin fine-dining dinner cost in Cappadocia?
faq.a: Expect roughly €90–€160 per person for tasting menus with wine pairings at Revithia, Nahita, or Lil'a, compared with €18–€35 per person for traditional testi kebab and meze in Göreme or Mustafapaşa.

faq.q: Are Avanos pottery workshops open on Sundays?
faq.a: Yes. Major family workshops and Güray Museum stay open seven days a week (generally 09:00–18:00), though smaller neighborhood studios along the river sometimes close on Sunday afternoons in winter.

faq.q: What is the best local breakfast dish to look for in Cappadocia?
faq.a: Look for kaymak (clotted cream) served with local Anatolian honeycomb, apricot preserves made from regional orchard fruit, fresh bazlama flatbread, and roasted pumpkin seeds (kabak çekirdeği), a Nevşehir specialty.
